The first screen is ready. You can open it here:

**http://maker:4001**

**Please try this:** In the box at the top, paste any web link you'd normally want to keep (for example `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bookmarking`) and press **Save**. Watch it appear in your list just below. Save one or two more if you like, then tell me how that first "save it and see it land in one place" moment feels.

A few things I decided for you here — please check whether each approach feels right:

- **Layout:** one simple page — a save box pinned at the top, and your saved links listed underneath it. Newest save appears at the top of the list.
- **How you save:** I set saving up as *paste the link, then press Save* — a single box, nothing else required. Is that the quick capture you had in mind, or would you expect to add something at save time (like a title or a note)?
- **What each saved item shows:** since you're only pasting a web address, I automatically make a short readable label from the link and show the full address underneath it. Please check whether that auto-label is good enough, or whether you'd want to type your own title.
- **Starting state:** before anything is saved, the page shows a friendly "nothing saved yet" prompt rather than a blank screen.

Once you're happy with this core save-and-see step, I'll build search on top of it next.
